comment: Every place this package's ESLint config deliberately differs from obsidian-dev-utils' shared config, and why.
This package is that package's sibling and resolves no dependency on it, so `scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a HAND
COPY - and a hand copy drifts silently, which it did for eighteen months. update-npm-deps.ps1 compares the two
configs on every dependency sweep and fails on anything not recorded here.
The comparison is DIRECTIONAL: only 'obsidian-dev-utils refined something and this copy never took it' is a
finding. A rule this package enables that obsidian-dev-utils turns off is printed as information and never fails,
because this copy is then the stricter one and obsidian-dev-utils' reasons for its own relaxations are
A key is the finding's identity exactly as the check prints it: <role>|<rule>|<kind>[|<detail>]. The
correspondence runs BOTH ways - an entry describing a divergence that no longer exists fails the sweep too, which
is what stops this file going stale the way the comments at the call sites did. Add `task` when the entry is an
adoption intended for later rather than a settled decision; it is then re-reported on every run.
`roles` names the file compared at each end. Only the `script` role is compared by default, because it is the one
role that plays the same part in both packages.

script|no-console|level.why: The build, lint, docs and version scripts are CLI entry points whose output IS their interface, so printing to stdout is what they are for. obsidian-dev-utils leaves the rule on everywhere because nothing in that package prints.

script|no-restricted-syntax|option|optio.why: Same selector, same severity - the message names this package's own escape hatch (`castTo<T>()` from src/internal/castTo.ts), which obsidian-dev-utils does not have and could not name.
Same selector, same severity - the wording says `in this project`, because here the mock classes really are the canonical types rather than one package's convention.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/no-over-cap-wa.why: This package vendors only the subset of obsidian-dev-utils' custom rules that applies to it; its plugin file's `rules` map IS that subset. This rule is about waits inside an Obsidian `eval`, which nothing here writes.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/require-compon.why: Not vendored - same subset reason. Obsidian `Component` subclasses are a plugin-authoring shape; this package mocks the API rather than building on it.

script|unicorn/class-reference-in-static.why: Every static factory here names its own class on purpose, and each mock class redeclares its factories rather than overriding an inherited one. Swapping the class name for `this` would make an inherited factory build the subclass while its signature still says the base, and `strictProxy(value, App)` passes the class as a runtime value, where `this` is a different object entirely.

script|unicorn/filename-case|option|opti.why: Source files are named after the API they mock, so the name is dictated by Obsidian and the DOM rather than by a casing convention - `Array.prototype.ts`, `App.ts`, `createEl.ts`. Allowing camel, kebab and pascal keeps the rule catching genuinely inconsistent names while preserving that 1:1 mapping.

script|unicorn/no-thenable|level.why: `Setting.then()` and `BaseComponent.then()` are Obsidian's own public API - the chainable callback hook every settings tab is written against. These mocks cannot drop a member of the surface they exist to reproduce.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-side-effects.why: Build, lint and version scripts are CLI entry points; the top-level call IS the program. Scoped to `scripts/**/*.ts`, beside the same block's `unicorn/no-process-exit` relaxation.
